title: Retired placements permanently reserve satellite capacity after re-enrollment
outcome: Retired placements retain their forensic records without permanently blocking fresh session admission after re-enrollment; current live reservations still enforce the declared capacity and stale placements acquire no new authority.
acceptance: A holder note identifies the placement capacity count, stale reservation filtering and completion authority paths, with source locators and the observed one-slot retired-placement counterexample.

A deterministic disposable-store regression shows a fresh root can be admitted at declared capacity one after the old reservation becomes retired by re-enrollment, while a current live reservation still blocks an additional admission. Admission accounting uses the executor reservation domain permanent-retirement boundary; transient disconnection, link-incarnation change, verification loss or settings changes alone do not free an unresolved current-enrollment reservation. Deterministic controls preserve current capacity limits and old records.
Old retired placement records and evidence remain preserved, and stale placement completion, binding or execution cannot gain authority through the accounting change.
The full gate passes on the exact final input that lands, with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding on that input.
